articles.headline: Texas' Justin Cryer makes himself right at home in Longhorns' win over rival Aggies
keyFacts: Texas senior linebacker Justin Cryer recorded a crucial late-game sack during the Longhorns' 16-6 victory over Texas A&M on Friday.
Texas coach Steve Sarkisian described the play as a huge sack that helped the defense secure the win.
Cryer, a January transfer from Florida State, celebrated his first appearance in the rivalry by joining the Longhorn Band after the game.
body: Texas linebacker Justin Cryer (28) reacts after sacking Texas A&M quarterback Brady Hart during an NCAA college football game in College Station, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle)
COLLEGE STATION - Justin Cryer knows plenty about the Texas-Texas A&M rivalry from his days growing up in the Katy area, but he didn't get his shot to play in it until his fourth year in college.
The man everyone calls "Juice" made sure to get the full experience.

The Texas Longhorns ' senior linebacker, who transferred from Florida State in January , took a lap around the grass inside Kyle Field hours before Friday night's game, wearing his coat and tie as well as an icy juice box pendant on the diamond chain around his neck. Then, he represented his team at midfield as one of the Longhorns' six captains.

Once the action started, there was Cryer again with a huge momentum-stemming sack. And, before his night was done, Cryer had found a spot on the stadium wall shortly after Texas' 16-6 win over Texas A&M , where he joined the Longhorn Band swinging and swaying to the music as all the maroon began to leak out of Kyle Field.
BOHLS: It's not always pretty, but Longhorns get it done

"It was dope," Cryer said of his first Aggies-Longhorns game. "Being able to run out there and all the tradition that they have here, it was cool to be a part of, and the best part about it: By the end of the game, everybody was gone except for the people in burnt orange."
Cryer, who starred at Brookshire Royal High School, had something to do with that hasty exit.

With Texas clinging to a 13-6 lead late in the third quarter, the Longhorns offense elected to stay on the field on a fourth-and-1 from the Aggies' 36. When Michael Terry III got stuffed the line, the 109,570 fans - the most at Kyle Field since 2021 - came to life.

However, just three plays later on a third-and-7 for Texas A&M, Cryer looped around the right side of the Aggies offensive line and came screaming around the corner where he found himself in the quarterback's lap before Brady Hart even knew he was there. The sack forced a punt and got the ball back to the Texas offense.
"That was a huge sack by Juice Cryer," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said.
JUSTIN CRYER SACKS BRADY HART 🤘 @InsideTexas || https://t.co/7PIa9sf9Mo https://t.co/rbhkkaPSKk

- Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 28, 2026 The sack didn't pay immediate dividends. Arch Manning took the Texas offense down the field, but then threw an interception in the end zone, putting the defense back out on the field. It delivered again, stopping the Aggies on a fourth down on Texas' side of the field, which led to a Longhorns field goal that finally put the game away.

"If there's a turnover or a punt or whatever (by the Texas offense), it doesn't matter, we're going to go back out there and make sure we get the ball back for our offense," Cryer said. "I love that mindset of this defense that no matter what situation we find ourselves in, we're going to do everything it takes to get the ball back for our offense."

Cryer was a freshman on the Florida State team that went 13-0 in the 2023 regular season, but still was left out of the College Football Playoff. He played a bigger role the next two seasons for Seminoles teams that went a combined 7-17. Transferring to Texas, which will be playing in its second SEC Championship Game since joining the conference three years ago, meant Cryer needed to adjust to higher expectations, especially playing for a defense that is one of the top in the nation while supporting an offense that often doesn't do it any favors.

"For someone who just got here in January, you've got to assimilate. You've got to get with the program or don't join at all," Cryer said. "Coach Sark has done a good job of building this identity along with (coordinator Will Muschamp) on defense. It's about how you respond. Not everything's going to go your way. You've got to show up and be at your best when your best is needed. On defense especially, we can't control what the other side of the ball does. All we can control is what we do, so if we have to win 3-0, we're going to win 3-0. It doesn't matter. We have a great mindset on defense. There's no complaining, and that's not common, that's not something that happens everywhere. Every time we set on the field, we're all trying to make a play for our offense."

And that's how Cryer, the younger brother of former UH basketball star and current Golden State Warrors guard L.J. Cryer, ended up on the railing inside Kyle Field celebrating a win over his team's biggest rival, even if he's been with the team for just 11 months.

"(Fellow linebacker Raheem Biles) is down for whatever and he said he was going up there, so if he was going up there, then I was going, too," Cryer said. "It was a fun atmosphere and the game lived up to the reputation. Glad to be a part of it."

articles.headline: Pensions and benefits services still down after 'cyber incident'
keyFacts: Online pensions and benefits services remained offline following a cyber incident that the Department for Work and Pensions took precautions to address.
The government stated that regular payments would continue and no personal information was believed to have been lost or stolen.
Authorities are investigating the incident in collaboration with the National Cyber Security Centre.
body: - Published
Online benefits and pensions services were still down on Saturday morning following a "cyber incident" which forced the government to take them offline.
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has not specified what triggered it to shut down access late on Thursday but has not ruled out that it was hit by hackers.

The government has assured benefits recipients and pensioners that their usual payments would continue to be made, though some people have reported delays and fear being penalised for missing deadlines to report information online.
The UK's former chief technology officer David Knott told BBC Newsnight his "strong suspicion" was that the department had been targeted by hackers.
He continued: "[The government has] taken down some of the citizen-facing services, which implies to me that there's some kind of attack could be mounted through the front door."

John Curry, a leading cyber security expert based at Bath Spa University, told BBC News the DWP had "almost certainly" detected hacking activity taking place and shut down its systems in an effort to stop data being stolen.
Curry said if the DWP had discovered hackers inside its computer systems, then the "best thing to do is slam the front door shut".

He also said the government may deliberately release limited information in order to "keep the enemy in the dark" and not give any possible hackers hints about ongoing work to secure sensitive systems.

On Friday, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said there had been a "serious cyber incident" without offering further details, while the department said the move to close online services was a "precaution".
Downing Street would not be drawn on whether the DWP had been targeted by hackers but did say other departments had not been accessed by a "malicious actor".
The government said it was working with GCHQ's National Cyber Security Centre to investigate the incident, which indicates a hack has not been ruled out.
The DWP makes around 2.5 million payments every day. Online portals for Pip applications and the "Tell Us Once" system for registering deaths have also been impacted.
The government also said on Friday that it did not believe any personal information had been lost or stolen.
The incident has fuelled concerns about the vulnerability of state computer systems and whether security protocols are keeping pace with advances in AI technology, which can be used to aid hackers.
Dame Chi Onwurah, chair of the House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, said the DWP incident should be a "wake-up call" for the government.

She continued: "People rely on these systems for some of the most essential services the state provides, and they should be able to trust that the tech and data underpinning them are secure and resilient."

Shadow AI minister Ben Spencer said the DWP incident was "deeply concerning", saying the government cannot "demand higher standards of cyber security from others without demonstrating that government are taking the necessary action to protect their own systems".
It is the latest in a run of global cyber incidents impacting government and major organisations, which have been variously triggered by hackers, faulty tech or botched upgrades.

articles.headline: Penn State rallies to beat Mississippi State in Battle 4 Atlantis
keyFacts: Penn State overcame a 16-point deficit to defeat Mississippi State 36-29 at halftime in the Battle 4 Atlantis in the Bahamas.
Ivan Juric set a program record with his eighth consecutive double-double to start the season, contributing 15 points and 17 rebounds.
Penn State will host UAlbany at the Bryce Jordan Center on Tuesday night for its next game.
body: The Penn State men's basketball team came through with a big second-half effort to leave the Bahamas with a win in the Battle 4 Atlantis. Ivan Juric set the program record for most consecutive double-doubles to start a season, and Penn State overcame a 16-point deficit to top Mississippi State on Friday night in Paradise Island, Bahamas.

Penn State trailed 36-29 at halftime but flipped the scoring output in the second half for the come-from-behind victory. Juric scored 15 points and a game-high 17 rebounds to help lead the way for the Nittany Lions . He also added four assists to lead the team and the game.

Penn State's defense turned things up on the Bulldogs in the comeback effort. The Bulldogs shot just 28.1% from the field in the second half. Mississippi State was held without a field goal in the final 6:30.

Dasonte Bowen had a big game for Penn State with a game-high 18 points on 7-of-12 shooting, including 2-for-2 from 3-point range. Penn State also drained 15 of 21 free throws, including 7-of-8 from Juric. Joining Juric and Bowen in double-digit scoring were Brant Byers with 13 points and Thomas Allard with 11 points.
Juric's double-double was the eitghth of the season. That sets a new school record for the most double-doubles to start a season, brekaing a tie with John Amaechi.

Penn State will return home to the Bryce Jordan Center for a couple of home games starting on Tuesday. The Nittany Lions host UAlbany in the Bryce Jordan Center on Tuesday night, Dec. 1, with a tipoff scheduled for 7:00 p.m.

articles.headline: Uganda starts mRNA Ebola vaccine trial in first for Africa
keyFacts: Uganda has started Africa's first clinical trial of an mRNA Ebola vaccine developed by Moderna to target the Bundibugyo strain.
The Uganda Virus Research Institute aims to enroll 224 volunteers, including children, to test vaccine safety and immune response.
A separate Ebola vaccine will begin testing in the DRC, with potential deployment expected by early 2027 if trials succeed.
body: Africa’s first clinical trial has begun in Uganda of an mRNA vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain behind a deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
The state-run Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI) said in a statement on Friday that the trial began in collaboration with Moderna, a United States-based company which manufactures the vaccine.
The Ugandan trial is the second for the vaccine, after Moderna began its first human trial of the shots in Canada in August, targeting adults from 18 to 65 years old.
UVRI said the Ugandan trial will for the first time test the vaccine’s safety and ability to trigger an immune response in children aged 1 year and above, and aims to enrol 224 volunteers.

“Children are often among those hardest hit when Ebola strikes, yet they ‌are too often the last to benefit from new vaccines,” said Richard Hatchett, chief executive officer of the Coalition ‌for ‌Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, which is helping fund the vaccine.
Other options

The other potential candidate for combating the Bundibugyo strain is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford. It will begin testing in the DRC on Monday.
But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting.

It signed a purchase commitment last week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and be approved by the World Health Organization and the DRC government.

Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, said he hoped trials of the drug would conclude in early 2027 and that, if successful, the purchase deal could move up deployment by months.
On Thursday, DRC government data showed that at least 12,021 Ebola infections have been confirmed, including 5,904 deaths since the outbreak began in mid-May.
Uganda declared its Ebola outbreak over on July 28. It had recorded 20 infections and two deaths, according to the Ministry of Health.

articles.headline: Nick Nurse reveals Joel Embiid is not 100% just yet after dealing with an illness
keyFacts: Joel Embiid returned to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup against the Indiana Pacers after missing games due to an illness.
Head coach Nick Nurse limited Embiid to 28 minutes to manage his conditioning and injury history.
Nurse stated that Embiid was a little winded and asked to come out during the game.
body: Joel Embiid has been dealing with an illness for the past week, which has led to him missing a couple of games. He returned to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup on Black Friday, but it seems that he was not yet at 100%.

The 76ers beat the Indiana Pacers 111-87, as Embiid played 28 minutes. He had a decent performance, getting 14 points, 11 rebounds, and three steals. It was an impressive performance, but 76ers head coach Nick Nurse knew that he had to be careful with Embiid's minutes.
Joel Embiid was not at 100% amid his return against the Pacers
For a star player like Embiid, it is important for a team to handle his minutes well. He has a long history with injuries and illnesses that will naturally need better treatment from the coaches.
Nurse was definitely thinking about that because he knows that Embiid will need to be 100% when the games become even more important.
It is still early in the season, which is why Nurse is allowing Embiid to build his rhythm moving forward. Fortunately for Embiid, he has a good coach who will take care of him when he needs it.

"Obviously, he was a little winded. Some short stints there, but I thought he looked good tonight... It was, cause he asked to come out a couple of times. That's the effect of the illness and conditioning. I thought he had some good plays, Nurse said after the 76ers' win against the Pacers.
Embiid will need to ramp it up soon if he wants to contribute for the 76ers. Thankfully, he has a lot of time left because the 76ers have an immense amount of talent with their players.

articles.headline: Fan shoves Luka Dončić after he flings his wristband at a woman in crowd
keyFacts: Los Angeles Lakers player Luka Dončić flung his wristband at a woman in the crowd after a loss to the Spurs on Friday.
Dončić stated that he returned to retrieve the wristband after hearing the woman did not want it, at which point a man with her shoved him.
Security guards quickly intervened after the shove, and the incident may require a response from the league.
body: The Los Angeles Lakers blew a 20-point lead in a loss to the Spurs on Friday, and Luka Dončić was not happy about it. Not only was this a gut-punch loss in a game for early dibs on the West's No. 1 seed, but Dončić has been ice cold from 3 over the last two-plus weeks (26 for 100) and it continued in San Antonio with a 1-for-13 showing.

This was at least the surface context under which a clearly frustrated Dončić walked off the court, and as he made his way toward the locker room he flung his wristband at a woman in the crowd. Moments later, Dončić turned around and went to retrieve the wristband, at which point the man who was with the woman handed it back to him and then shoved the Lakers superstar before multiple security guards quickly intervened.

"I just threw my wristband, like I do almost every game," Doncic explained. "Then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it and then he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else."

The reporter asked if the fan had said anything to Dončić that perhaps instigated the wristband fling, or if there were words after the shove (which there pretty clear were), but Dončić stuck to his innocent explanation of what appeared to be a pretty aggressive act on his part.

Luka Dončić was asked about the fan shoving him after the game. He said that he tossed his wrist band to a fan and then heard them say they don't want it, so he returned to get it and then got shoved. pic.twitter.com/7mBjXKWbAD
— Jared Weiss (@JaredWeissNBA) November 28, 2026

If you watch the video again, you can pretty clearly see the woman saying something to Doncic before he flings the wristband. Maybe she was trash talking him. Or, maybe she was responding to the middle finger that Doncic appeared to flip toward the crowd moments before.
Cameras caught Luka Dončić FLIPPING OFF and then casually tossing his wristband at an older female Spurs fan. He then walked back to snatch it away.
That is when the fan’s angry husband stepped in and shoved him. 👀 https://t.co/aKESpD7Qnm pic.twitter.com/eZpioMSyqe
— SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) November 28, 2026

Either way, this is not a good look for Dončić. That was not a fan-friendly wristband giveaway, as Doncic wants you to believe. That is a back-turned slingshot at an elderly woman. If that's how he hands out wristbands after games (heaven forbid to a little kid), by slinging it into their chest as he keeps right on walking by, he's got some real growing up to do.

Even if these people were taunting Doncic, he can't do that. We'll see if any further explanation as to what was said in this exchange surfaces, but at first glance this looks like Luka, for whatever reason, firing a wristband in frustration at a woman, and a man next to her taking offense to that aggression, hence the shove.
This definitely feels like an incident the league is going to have to address.

articles.headline: Explosive Fury vs Klitschko canvas row revisited
keyFacts: On November 28, 2015, Tyson Fury nearly cancelled his heavyweight title fight against Wladimir Klitschko due to an explosive dispute over a spongy ring canvas.
Fury's team and promoter argued the thick layers would prevent his movement and endanger health, while Vitali Klitschko defended the conditions as equal.
Klitschko's team removed the offending layers after Fury's camp threatened to walk away, allowing Fury to win the bout and change the division's course.
body: Tyson Fury vs Wladimir Klitschko: Revisit the furious canvas row that changed the course of the heavyweight division

On November 28 in 2015 Tyson Fury toppled the man who had dominated the heavyweight division when he beat Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf; But he almost had to scuttle the contest on the day of the fight in an explosive row over the ring surface, which saw Vitali Klitschko weighing in
Thursday 26 November 2026 15:15, UK
On this day in 2015 Tyson Fury scaled his Everest. He dethroned Wladimir Klitschko, the dominant heavyweight of that era, to win the unified WBO, IBF and WBA world heavyweight championships.
It was the goal Fury had targeted throughout his career. Klitschko had ruled the division for a decade and was selling out stadiums in Germany.
Fury travelled to Dusseldorf as the underdog but utterly confident he had the tools to unravel Klitschko.
However on the day of the fight, an explosive row at the Esprit Arena threatened to scuttle the whole event.

Peter Fury, Tyson's uncle and then trainer, decided he wanted to inspect the ring in advance. Then they spotted something they hadn't expected. Feeling the canvas, they realised that the layers under it were spongy.
Tyson Fury climbed through the ropes to bounce on the balls of his feet on the canvas where he was due, a few hours later, to stage a remarkable win.
"No way you can fight on that," his father John Fury said.
"You know what they've done that for," the then heavyweight title challenger said, "so I can't move."

Speaking to the camera, Tyson Fury declared: "They must have half a foot deep of sponge on the canvas. It's like training on a beach on the sand. It's absolutely ridiculous and I can tell you now, Sky Sports viewers, there's no fight if that ring ain't sorted.
"I'm a mover and I move, that's the way I fight. I can't move in that ring."

History could have been very different. If he'd gone ahead with the fight, he could - probably would - have lost. He certainly wouldn't have been able to box in the way he did so successfully later that night.
"My fighter is not fighting in quicksand," his trainer Peter Fury declared at the time.
They undid the ring canvas to look underneath; there were two soft layers that they insisted had to be removed.

Vitali Klitschko, Wladimir's older brother and a fearsome former world heavyweight champion himself, was on hand to respond. He stood in the ring himself, towering over the top rope and glowering down at Fury's team on the floor of the arena.
Mick Hennessy, Fury's promoter, told him: "You're trying to control this but it's not in the interest of health and safety. So we need it sorted.
"Your ankle or your knee could go on this, it's too thick."
Vitali, a formidable advocate for his brother, argued fiercely, gesturing animatedly as he said: "Both fighters have the same conditions. Same gloves, same ring and you're unhappy always.
"Everything you say is excuses," he roared. "Do you want to fight or not?"
Fury's team weren't bluffing though. They were prepared to walk away.
John Fury raged at Bernd Boente, Klitschko's manager, in a corridor at the arena. He told him directly: "The fight's off, forget about it." Then he stormed off.
He later said: "If they hadn't replaced it, there wouldn't have been a fight."

Fury's team got their way. The offending layers were removed and Fury did indeed use his footwork and mobile long-range boxing to defuse Klitschko, a dangerous puncher, so adept normally at controlling distance but who just couldn't pin down an inspired Fury.

That blazing row did change the course of the heavyweight division. It was an important element in a monumental victory for the Englishman. Fury became the dominant figure in the weight class. He was unable to meet Klitschko again in a rematch; struggling with depression, he stepped away from the sport.
But Fury's mental health improved and he was able to make a famous comeback. He cemented his legend against Deontay Wilder, becoming a two-time heavyweight world champion without losing a fight.
Now he has the chance to become a three-time champion when he fights his great rival Anthony Joshua for the first time with a vacant WBA title on the line.
That climactic fight is two weeks away as Fury looks to start the final chapter in a championship story that began 11 years ago today.

articles.headline: 'It doesn't come from me' - Eckert irked by Southampton jibes at Boro
keyFacts: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert stated that taunts aimed at Middlesbrough did not originate from him.
Southampton defeated Middlesbrough 2-0 in a match featuring pre-game provocation videos and post-match tension.
Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg said that Southampton player Finn Azaz should have handled his celebration differently.
body: - Published
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has stressed that taunts from the club aimed at Championship opponents Middlesbrough did not come from him.
Saints beat the league leaders 2-0 on Friday night, scoring twice in the second half while keeping a clean sheet in a fiery game at St Mary's.

On Friday morning, the club posted a much talked about video recalling the play-off campaign last season and how success was "ours... until it wasn't" before Middlesbrough "got another go", followed by footage of Oli McBurnie's winner for Hull at Wembley.
Eckert - who was at the centre of the Spygate scandal that led to Southampton being expelled from the play-offs in May - revealed after Friday's game that he did not like the video.
He said he had not been aware that it would be played before kick-off
Saints fans cheered as McBurnie's winner hit the back of the net on the big screens.
The match ended with the song Stop Crying Your Heart Out by Oasis ringing out as Middlesbrough's players left the field.
A box of tissues was also conveniently placed on the media conference table after the match, before Eckert removed it once made aware it was next to him.
"I just hope that we can do everything that we do with class," an exasperated Eckert said after the game.
"I hope that everyone that came here, especially the Middlesbrough staff and players, know that these things don't come from me.

"I think that everything you do in victory or defeat should be with class and I try to do that. I hope that there's an appreciation that this doesn't come from me and I'll make sure that Kim [Hellberg, Middlesbrough's head coach] knows this.
"I hope this doesn't become a big topic as the football game was so good today, I respect Kim and Middlesbrough a lot."
Tensions spilled over during the game, as former Middlesbrough player Finn Azaz ran the length of the field to celebrate in front of Boro supporters late in the game.
Supporters had to be held back as they tried to enter the field, as the Saints attacker made a crying gesture in their direction.
He later justified his celebration by sharing that it was a response to Boro fans singing about his family in games last season.
Hellberg said that he felt Azaz should have handled the situation differently.
"It's always a thing that you have as a footballer and a coach to try to be a role model," Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees.
"Be better. I know it's sometimes tough with emotions sometimes. I said to [Azaz that] it wasn't a good move.

"I know players, whatever they are, are young people and sometimes get their emotions into it, which you sometimes have to have respect for. But you can handle it and should handle it in a better way."

articles.headline: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
keyFacts: The number of Indian workers subject to social security contributions in Germany has grown to over 140,000 professionals over the past decade, according to DW.
Observers note that German companies and workers' councils often hesitate to hire from India due to high language requirements and fears of wage-dumping.
Experts warn that some third-country nationals face exploitation and recruitment scams when entering the German labor market through EU mobility loopholes.
body: Pratyay Saikia was studying food technology in 2022 when he saw an advertisement from Magic Billion, a recruitment agency that places skilled and semi-skilled Indian professionals in verified jobs abroad.
The 25-year-old from the northern Indian state of Haryana reached out to explore employment opportunities.
Four years later, he is working as a butcher at Metzgerei Lederer in southern Germany, having completed a three-year apprenticeship at the butcher shop.

"I came to Baden-Württemberg with 180 other Indians who came here to do an Ausbildung [apprenticeship] program. Me and seven others did our Ausbildung at Lederer [butcher shop], while others went into the construction sector. I now have a full-time job here," Saikia told DW.
He is not alone as the number of Indian workers subject to social security contributions in Germany has grown sevenfold over the past decade, to over 140,000 professionals.
Many of them work in the IT and health care sectors.
Pressing need for workers, but hesitant to hire

Germany, facing a shrinking and rapidly aging population, doesn't just need software specialists and nurses. It is also seeking skilled professionals such as electricians, mechatronics technicians, solar panel installers and truck drivers.

A 2024 study by Bertelsmann Foundation concluded that Germany needs 288,000 foreign skilled workers per year until 2040 to fill the shortage left by retiring workers. Another report from the consulting firm FMC Group noted that over 369,000 skilled job positions went unfilled in 2025.

Despite the pressing need for skilled workers, many firms, particularly Germany's renowned Mittelstand (small and medium-sized enterprises), are reluctant to recruit from places like India, say observers.

"Hiring an electrician from India is a relatively new concept for German companies, so they are hesitant," said Daniel Raja, managing director of NM NextMittelstand GmbH, a Düsseldorf-based recruitment firm focused on connecting German firms with skilled workers from India.
The Mittelstand companies are often overlooked by young talent abroad, while many of these firms are not actively recruiting international skilled workers, Raja said.
This disconnect, coupled with the often high German language requirements, means that many skilled positions remain unfilled, he explained.
Language a key hurdle
Saikia, the butcher, had studied German to the B1 level, considered intermediate proficiency. He soon realized it was not enough for everyday communication at work.

"Initially, I found the theory classes of my Ausbildung quite difficult. But my co-workers helped me. After one year, my German improved, and I realized integration happened automatically as my language level improved," he said.
David Kipp, researcher in the Global Issues Research Group at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), said he's "skeptical" about lowering language requirements.

"Language skills are an important selection criterion so people actually know where they are going. Sending people with very little language knowledge makes exploitation easier, because they have less direct contact with German institutions," he told DW.
Language, however, isn't the only hurdle.
Raja said workers' councils also often resist hiring from abroad.

"Company decisions in the Mittelstand involve the team and the shop floor," he pointed out. "In some cases, the workers' council resists hiring from India because they mistakenly believe 'cheap Indian labor' will take their jobs or undercut their wages."
Raja said he often uses unconventional outreach methods, including hosting TikTok Live sessions, to engage directly with industrial employers and workers and dispel concerns and misconceptions.
Exploiting the EU mobility loophole?
German companies have traditionally relied on workers from Central and Eastern European (CEE) nations such as Poland, Romania and Slovenia to fill labor market gaps.
But studies show CEE workers are increasingly reluctant to relocate to Germany, as faster economic growth and stronger career prospects improve opportunities in their home countries.
The situation has prompted recruitment agencies in these countries to look beyond the European Union for workers.

These third-country nationals (TCNs) obtain residence permits in CEE states and are then posted to German job sites under the Vander Elst visa. The mechanism allows non-EU citizens legally employed in one EU member state to be temporarily sent to work in another.

"European Labour Authority's (ELA) 2025 study on the posting of third-country nationals found that the number of posted TCNs is increasing. The main sectors concerned are construction and transport," said Pia Fallstrom, ELA spokesperson.
The exact number of TCNs posted across the EU is difficult to gauge, as data exchange between sending and receiving countries by nationality and sector is limited.
"Finding out how blue-collar workers get here really requires fieldwork," said Kipp, noting that Indian recruiters are aware of this mobility loophole and take advantage of these opportunities.
While there are regulations to protect workers posted to Germany from another EU state, ELA said the practice has often led to wage-dumping.

"ELA's work has identified issues such as difficulties accessing information on applicable rules, complex subcontracting arrangements, letterbox companies, bogus self-employment and other cases of non-compliance," noted Fallstrom.
"Posted third-country nationals can be particularly vulnerable because they may also depend on their employer for their work and residence permits."
Raja said he had seen cases of workers falling victim to recruitment scams and being exploited as a result.

"I know of a family that took out a loan so that their child could enroll in an institute which promised a job in Germany," said Raja. "When the candidate realized it's a scam, they ended up in Bahrain doing a tough manual labor job just to pay off the loan."
What to do to prevent exploitative hiring practices?
Saikia, the butcher, stressed the importance of workers verifying that a recruitment agency is legitimate.
In his case, he said the agency's detailed website and its CEO's willingness to speak with him during the early stages of the recruitment process gave him confidence that it was not a scam.

Kipp, the SWP expert, argued that preventing exploitative hiring practices requires streamlining migration procedures, expanding pre-departure cultural training and becoming more effective at identifying trusted entities and combating social media scams.
"India is the most important country for experimenting with how work migration functions. If we don't pay attention, we'll just send people into the low-wage sector and into disappointment," he said.

articles.headline: 5 Unnecessary Nintendo Switch 2 Accessories to Buy Yourself Before Black Friday Ends
keyFacts: IGN published a list of unnecessary Nintendo Switch 2 accessories that are currently discounted for Black Friday sales.

body: Nintendo has been having some of the best Black Friday video game deals this year. Walmart was even dropping $30 first-party Switch 2 game deals at one point, and there's plenty of other discounts worth checking out if you haven't already. But if you already have a Switch 2 and plenty of games, what good are these discounts to you? If you've had your console since day one, you may be looking to add some extra accessories to your collection instead.

I'm not talking about necessary accessories like controllers and gaming headsets , though. I'm talking about the stuff that you don't actually need to enjoy your gaming experience. I'm here to shine a light on the accessories that are truly extra in all the best ways.

Warning : You may not need these items, but you'll probably end up wanting them. And because they are all on sale for Black Friday, the temptation to buy them will be greater than ever. Proceed with scrolling at your own risk.
Retro Switch Game Case

Let's start with one of my favorites, this Game Boy-inspired Switch 2 game case. This bad boy can hold up to three cartridges and three microSD Express cards at any given time. So you could likely hold most of your game library in this thing if so inclined. It is definitely less safe to put all of your games on a keychain, rather than an actual protective case, but who cares about safety when you've got that retro gaming style working its magic.
Master Sword Game Card Holder/Sword Grip

Of all of the Switch accessories I've seen in my life, this one never fails to make me laugh. It's trying to solve multiple problems that don't actually exist while also attempting to appeal to fans of The Legend of Zelda. The Master Sword design is compatible with the Joy-Con 2 controller and is meant to be used with Skyward Sword HD , Tears of the Kingdom, and Switch Sports Chambara. On top of that, you're able to store 12 games in this thing for no reason at all.
I still think this is a very silly thing, but I almost buy it every time it's on sale. I don't even know where I'd put this thing.
Basecase for Switch 2 Gaming Pillow

Now that we've gotten the silly card holders out of the way, let's get to the things that solve those first-world problems. If you've spent a good bit of time playing your Switch 2 in handheld mode, then you likely know about "the tingles". This is that funny feeling at your elbows telling you that your arms are not properly being utilized for their biological purpose. If you want those weird feelings (and existential thoughts) to be banished forever, this Switch 2 gaming pillow is great for that.
My coworker actually tested out a pillow just like this one and said it was surprisingly awesome.
Spigen JoyCon Grips

Have you ever had to use a Joy-Con as an actual controller? If you're used to using a Switch Pro controller , it's just going to feel wrong. My nephew always wants to play Super Smash Bros. whenever the family gets together, but he only has one good controller and the rest of us are left with what is essentially half of a remote to play with. I still usually win, but it's getting more difficult every time. If I had one of these grips, using the Joy-Con in this manner would definitely feel less awkward.
DIY GameCube Shell and Buttons for Switch 2 Pro Controller

Last but not least, arguably the least necessary accessory there is — a purely stylistic change. After a full year of the Nintendo Switch 2 being on the market, there's a surprising lack of special edition Switch 2 controllers available to buy. So if you want something that better fits your style, I propose taking the DIY route. This GameCube-inspired shell and buttons will transform your controller into an early 2000s fever dream. The only downside is that you'll need to be able to take apart (and reassemble) your Switch 2 Pro Controller to get the look. Still cheaper than buying a new controller.

articles.headline: 7 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Food
keyFacts: Polygon published a list featuring seven of cartoonist Gary Larson's funniest 'Far Side' comics that star food.
The selected comic strips include surreal concepts such as a sandwich mafia, potato salad crime, and a chef using his shoe to make soup.
The article highlights how Larson combined lowbrow and highbrow humor, dark themes, and inanimate objects coming to life.
body: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic. While most of them featured stupid humans or talking animals as their main characters, the surrealist streak in cartoonist Gary Larson sometimes gave life to inanimate objects as well. For example, there’s a strip where a jogger tells a living pair of scissors that they can no longer run together. And if scissors can be alive in The Far Side comics, just about anything can, including food.
Here are the seven funniest Far Side comics that star food, some of which feature food that has even gained sentience for the sake of a perfect joke.

I love this comic strip because it is just unabashedly silly. Not only are sandwiches alive in this one-panel reality, but they have such a complex social structure that they even have their own organized crime. The sandwich mafia is so cruel that it punishes its victims by hurling them into a pit of fourth-graders. If I were the sandwich, I’d be especially worried about the fourth-grader in the green stripey shirt. He looks vicious.
Yet another food item that has turned to a life of crime. Here, Larson interprets potato salad going bad in the silliest way possible.

This is a twist on that classic gag where, with two people in a life boat, one begins to imagine the other as food. This one features a man and a cow in a lifeboat, so the man naturally imagines steak while looking at the cow. As for the cow, well, he dreams of the man as a pile of man-shaped grass.

I love how adorable-looking these man-eating bears are as they stumble upon a group of campers in sleeping bags and exclaim “Sandwiches!” Personally, I think of sleeping bags as more burrito-like or even more like pita bread than sandwiches, but perhaps these bears aren’t terribly educated about the ways other cultures eat.

One of the reasons why The Far Side endures more than 30 years after Gary Larson concluded his strip is that he never spoke down to his audience. Sure, he had some dumb jokes sometimes, but they were never dumbed down for our sake; they were just dumb for the sake of being dumb — like a sandwich mafia. Larson could pull off the lowbrow and the highbrow, often in the very same comic, as this one illustrates.

At a glance, it doesn’t even seem like there’s a joke here, despite the simple caption: “Soup of the day is ready!” This is one of those comic strips by Larson that demands that you go looking for the punchline. Larson seems to trust that the audience will find the joke (or maybe he doesn’t care if some don’t, which I applaud). Eventually, you see that this chef is missing his shoe, meaning he used it to make the soup. So for all that highbrow thinking you had to do to find the punchline, the joke is incredibly lowbrow. It’s the perfect mix.

Larson also got into really dark humor at times. He once drew a comic strip where a snake killed himself by becoming his own noose, which is both silly and incredibly macabre. Yet this food-centric panel is so dark that it borders on creepy. Who is this guy that wants to buy this young employee of the butcher? And who is this butcher that is willing to sell him?

I first read this comic strip when I was a teenager, around the time when I first discovered The Far Side and quickly became obsessed with it. Since then, every time I make a waffle, I cannot help but think of this comic strip. I’ll mix the batter, spray the waffle iron, pour the mix in, close the top, and wait for that little light to go off. Inevitably, as I’m staring at that little light, I’ll murmur, “Slave to the waffle light.” It's one of those pieces of art that just speaks to a real-life truism.
When making waffles, we are all Wendell Zurkowitz.

articles.headline: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
keyFacts: Eight military personnel died in a Peruvian military helicopter crash in a remote drug-trafficking region.
The Peruvian ministry of defence stated that the pilot was the sole survivor and was evacuated for medical treatment.
The aircraft crashed during a mission to evacuate an army patrol in an area known as Cocaine Valley.
body: - Published
Eight military personnel have been killed in a helicopter crash in a remote area of Peru known for growing and trafficking drugs.

Authorities say the aircraft came down near the town of Sanabamba during a mission to evacuate an army patrol in the valley of the Apurimac, Ene, and Mantaro rivers, known by its Spanish acronym VRAEM.
Often referred to as 'Cocaine Valley', the area is Peru's largest coca-growing valley where gangs and the remnants of the former Shining Path rebel group operate.
The Peruvian ministry of defence said the pilot was the sole survivor of the crash, the cause of which is still unknown.
In its statement, the ministry said "search and rescue operations located the aircraft and the nine military personnel who were on board".
It named the pilot as Enzo Espinoza Roque and said he was evacuated to Lima to "receive specialised medical treatment".
The aircraft was reported missing on Thursday night after rescuing three army personnel.
No further information was shared about why the group needed to be rescued, but it was confirmed that they were among those who were killed in the crash.

Joint Command of the Peruvian Armed Forces posted a tribute online extending "deepest condolences to the family members, friends, and comrades-in-arms of the members of our VRAEM Special Command who lost their lives while carrying out a military mission. May God keep them in His glory".
In February, a MI-17 helicopter crashed in southern Peru in February killing all 15 on board.
Peru, along with Colombia, is one of the world's largest producers of coca leaves and cocaine, according to the United Nations.

body: New York State Sen. Andrea Stewart-Cousins, a Democrat , died Thursday evening, a state official announced on Friday.
Stewart-Cousins, 76, was reelected earlier this month as the top Democrat in the Empire State’s Senate. The circumstances of her death are unclear.

“It is with profound sadness that I announce the passing of New York State Senate Temporary President and Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins,” New York Senate majority spokesman Mike Murphy said in a statement.

“Serving the people of the 35th Senate District was one of the greatest honors of her life,” Murphy added. “Throughout her decades in public service, Stewart-Cousins made a profound impact on the lives of New Yorkers.”

Then-New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, right, signs Reproductive Health Act Legislation during a ceremony, Tuesday, Jan. 22, 2019, in the Red Room at the State Capitol in Albany, New York. (Darren McGee/Office of Gov. Andrew Cuomo via AP)
Stewart-Cousins was also the first black woman to lead the state Senate and one of the highest-ranking black women in state history.

The longtime state senator leaves behind a long legacy of firsts. After losing her initial bid for state Senate by only 18 votes in 2004, she ran again two years later and won. Soon after, in 2012, she became the first woman to lead a legislative conference in the New York State House, serving as the Democratic leader.
Stewart-Cousins made history again in 2019, when she became the first woman to serve as New York Senate majority leader, with a brief stint as president in January.

The Democratic Party won its largest majority in recent history in the 2026 midterm elections earlier this month. The state’s upper chamber captured at least 47 seats in the 63-seat chamber, giving it a veto-proof supermajority.

But today, I’m grieving a friend who meant so much to me and whom I admired more than she could have ever known.”

articles.headline: For critics, Trump presidency enters new walls-closing-in stage
keyFacts: Critics and commentators are reviving claims that the walls are closing in on President Trump following midterm losses and upcoming Democratic congressional investigations.
Writer Nick Catoggio and author Michael Wolff suggested that Trump's intervention in the Nvidia CEO case could lead to impeachment and conviction.
Polling analyst Nate Silver stated that betting markets indicate a 25% chance that Trump will be impeached and removed from office.
body: FOR CRITICS, TRUMP PRESIDENCY ENTERS NEW WALLS-CLOSING-IN STAGE. Do you remember Donald Trump’s first term as president, when the pursuers trying to bring him down would proclaim that victory was near, that the “walls were closing in,” and that Trump would soon fall? It happened all the time, often in relation to what Trump called the “Russia, Russia, Russia” affair, but also in matters relating to the Ukraine impeachment, former fixer Michael Cohen’s testimony against Trump, and many other hair-on-fire controversies of the day.

To save the tedium of repeating a long list of examples, here is a video compilation of 40 or so instances of politicians, pundits, and journalists declaring that the walls were closing in on Trump between 2017 and 2023. Only after Trump made a historic comeback to win the presidency a second time did his adversaries have to concede that the walls had not, in fact, closed in on him.
Recommended Stories

There was much less of that kind of talk in the first two years of Trump’s return. The reasons were clear: Trump had totally vanquished his antagonists, winning the popular vote for the White House, plus Republican majorities in the House and Senate. Jack Smith, the prosecutor appointed by the Biden administration to indict Trump, had to give up in frustration. And once Trump took office, no special prosecutor arrived to play the role that Robert Mueller played in the first term.

Trump began his second time in office with a far-reaching flex of executive authority, then passed an equally far-reaching spending and deregulation bill, and, for a time, seemed in total command of Washington.

But now, with an unresolved mess in Iran, catastrophic midterm losses, and the arrival of large Democratic majorities in both houses of Congress, Trump is in an obviously weaker position. Democratic chairmen who haven’t even taken office yet are outlining the targets of investigations that will begin in 2027. Whoever their immediate target is, they are all ultimately aimed at Trump.

And now, before the action has begun, the walls-are-closing-in talk has returned. Some are even using those exact words. In any event, the message is clear: Trump’s bad deeds are finally catching up to him.

In the Dispatch, Nick Catoggio pointed to Trump’s intervention in the firing and reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in the Chinese spy matter as the “Big One” that will bring Trump down once and for all. “By ‘Big One,’ I mean that Huang’s treachery and the administration’s complicity in it are the scandal that seems likely to finally swallow Trump,” Catoggio wrote.

Catoggio knows the history: “For 10 years, the president’s critics have looked forward to the day that his promiscuous malfeasance would bring him down — only to end up each time like Wile E. Coyote running into a painted tunnel. Access Hollywood didn’t do it; Russiagate didn’t do it; January 6 didn’t do it; four criminal indictments didn’t do it.” Yet now is different, Catoggio concluded: “More so than any previous scandal, this one looks poised to do it. … The word ‘treason’ is used too often and too lightly in political polemics, but if all of this is as bad as it looks, that’s the neighborhood in which this scandal lives.”

Author Michael Wolff, an informal adviser to the late Jeffrey Epstein who made a splash with a sensational book on the first Trump White House, recently said that the Nvidia matter “may be quite a straightforward case for impeachment and conviction.” Wolff alleged that the case involved both treason and bribery, the only two specific crimes mentioned in the Constitution as grounds for impeachment and removal of a president.

Also on the question of impeachment, polling analyst Nate Silver recently said he agreed with betting markets that indicated there is a 25% chance Trump will be both impeached and removed from office before his term is over. “Like, there’s no bottom here,” Silver said on the Still Counting podcast. Trump’s job approval rating could fall further, Silver added, “And like, if he’s doing s*** like profit off selling advanced chips to China, abso-f***ing-lutely literally he could be [impeached and removed]. And he should be. He should be.”

In mid-September, Trump had a bad string of luck — the Federal Reserve raised interest rates, he lost a court case or two, gas prices kept rising — that seemed pretty much par for the course as he headed toward midterm defeat. Nevertheless, some commentators saw something larger.

“We all knew that this day would come,” former federal Judge Michael Luttig said on MS Now. “Right now, today, the walls are closing in on Donald Trump.” At around the same time, Axios CEO Jim VandeHei reported, “The president feels the walls are caving in.” A month later, as the election neared, former CNN anchor Don Lemon titled his podcast episode, “The Walls are Closing In and Trump’s Running Out of Time.”
So far, there have been nowhere near the number of “walls are closing in” pronouncements that there were in Trump’s first term. But it’s beginning. Again.

Will it turn out the same way, with Trump reenacting the Road Runner-Wile E. Coyote scene over and over? Maybe — it wouldn’t be a bad bet. On the other hand, the fact that the walls did not close in during Trump’s first term does not mean they will not close in during his second. Trump often expresses confidence that things will be fine: “Bottom line, it’s all going to work out. You know why? It always does.” So far it has. But there are no guarantees.

articles.headline: Mamdani handed out $95K in staff raises the same day he warned of $12B budget deficit: report
keyFacts: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved roughly $850,000 in pay raises for dozens of City Hall aides during his first year in office, payroll records showed.
On Jan. 28, five City Hall employees received raises totaling $95,000 on the same day Mamdani warned of an estimated $12 billion budget deficit.
City Hall did not immediately return a request for comment from Fox News Digital regarding the justifications for the early salary increases.
body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved roughly $850,000 in pay raises for dozens of City Hall aides during his first year in office, according to municipal payroll records reviewed by the New York Post .
The records show the raises were distributed to at least 46 staffers since Mamdani took office in January, bringing total compensation increases near $1 million.

The Post counted 21 new hires who received raises totaling $450,000 before their first anniversary on the job, more than twice the combined number of first-year employees who got raises under Eric Adams and Bill de Blasio.
MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS

On Jan. 28, five City Hall employees were granted salary increases totaling $95,000 on the same day Mamdani announced New York City faced an estimated $12 billion budget deficit, the records show. The mayor’s office later lowered that projected deficit to approximately $5.4 billion.
The mayor’s office on Nov. 12 confirmed the city’s fiscal 2027 budget rose $3.3 billion from the budget adopted in June, reaching $129.2 billion.
MAMDANI'S TAXPAYER-FUNDED INFLUENCER ARMY ACCUSED OF PLOTTING PRESSURE CAMPAIGN AGAINST NYC CEOS
The payroll disclosures detail significant salary adjustments across several executive staff positions.

Julia Simcoe and Jacob Russell each received raises of more than $60,000, bringing their salaries to $148,000 and $145,000, respectively, the Post reported. Three other City Hall staffers received raises ranging from $30,000 to $45,000.
MAMDANI’S AFFORDABILITY REVOLUTION STUMBLED AS RENT COSTS SOAR TO RECORD HIGHS
The salary increases come as Mamdani, who took office Jan. 1 as the city's first self-described socialist mayor, faces fiscal constraints and administrative hurdles on core campaign pledges.

Mamdani’s plan to eliminate bus fares across the five boroughs has stalled after pushback from New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who noted the Metropolitan Transportation Authority cannot absorb the loss of revenue from fare boxes. While Mamdani’s campaign estimated the initiative would cost $700 million, the New York City Independent Budget Office (IBO) projected that fully eliminating fares would cost New York State roughly $1.1 billion.
EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

The administration has also faced capacity limits with its universal childcare initiative. A pilot program aimed at 2-year-olds launched with 2,000 available seats but drew more than 5,700 applicants, leaving roughly 3,700 children on waitlists. The program cost $73 million to launch, and the IBO estimated an expanded citywide version would cost $425 million by 2028.

Meanwhile, Mamdani's plan to establish five city-run grocery stores that sell items 30% below market value has drawn skepticism from retail analysts and economists who question whether the discounts can be sustained without ongoing taxpayer subsidies.

Fox News Digital asked the mayor's office what civil service guidelines justified the early salary bumps, why raises were authorized the same day Mamdani warned of a $12 billion deficit and how City Hall reconciles the payroll increases with budget constraints on programs like universal childcare and free transit.
A spokesperson for City Hall did not immediately return a request for comment.
Fox News Digital’s Leo Briceno contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Apple Stays Winning as Smartphone Sales Continue to Slump
keyFacts: Global smartphone sales fell 9% in the third quarter of 2026 due to rising memory costs driven by AI data center expansion, according to Counterpoint Research.
Apple increased its market share from 50% to 57%, while competitors with cheaper phone lineups saw declines because they struggled to absorb component costs.
Counterpoint predicts smartphone sales will remain weak next quarter as consumers increasingly choose second-hand devices or wait for major holiday deals.
body: RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.

According to a new report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025. The report attributed the drop to rising memory costs, which are hurting sales at the low end of the Android phone market.

In terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline. Where did those sales go, you might be wondering? Unsurprisingly, Apple’s broad range of iPhone models — from the 17E to its newest foldable flagship, the $1,999 iPhone Duo — bumped the company’s share of the smartphone market from 50% to 57% since last year.
More from CNET

Smartphone-makers with cheaper phone lineups suffered due to component costs, particularly memory, eating into their margins. “There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Emily Herbert.

The slowdown in phone sales has been happening all year. In the last quarter, the market slumped by 20%, more than was expected at the time. The build-out of data centers to support the ever-expanding AI industry has led to shortages of memory components. In turn, the prices of those components have spiked, raising prices of not just smartphones, but game consoles, PCs and other electronics.
Read more: Best Black Friday iPhone Deals
Will the holidays save smartphone-makers?

Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the Christmas gift-giving season typically mean strong phone sales for companies like Apple and Samsung. But the memory component crisis isn’t going to go away that quickly, and prices of phones are still higher overall.

Counterpoint predicts that smartphone sales will remain weak in the next quarter and that US carriers may be more selective about the promotions they offer this year. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are also seeing declining sales and customers are getting choosier about committing to phones that often cost more than $1,000. People are also looking to second-hand and refurbished phones instead of buying new.

“Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne. “This year’s holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual.”

articles.headline: 5 ways to make sure your console isn't holding back your GTA 6 performance
keyFacts: Xbox owners found a trick to break the 30 fps cap in GTA 6 by toggling display output and using Quick Resume, but Digital Foundry testing showed it causes game animations to run too fast and averages only about 36 fps.
Rockstar's technology production director Marc Chambers stated that even the PS5 Pro's processor is not powerful enough to run native 40 or 60 fps modes.
Rockstar released the first post-launch update for GTA 6 on November 23 to fix crashing and progression bugs, though the patch notes did not mention any performance or frame rate improvements.
body: 5 ways to make sure your console isn't holding back your GTA 6 performance
GTA 6 already pushes every PS5 and Xbox to its limit, but is yours falling short of it?

Within days of GTA 6's November 19 debut, Xbox owners had found a way to break its 30 fps cap. The trick, which was first reported on November 22, involves flipping a Series X's output between 60Hz and 120Hz, then hopping in and out of the game using Quick Resume. It works... sort of. When Digital Foundry tested the trick, it found the uncapped Series X averaged about 36 fps over an hour of play. The game's cars and animations also moved noticeably faster than they're meant to (some at around double speed).

It's fundamentally the processor that's holding GTA 6 at 30 fps on current-gen consoles (PS5 Pro included). The fact that a Series X with the limiter switched off is only able to find six extra frames per second illustrates how little is left to play with, so tinkering with settings isn't going to do very much. What you can do, however, is check whether your console is making the most of its available hardware.

A system that's out of date, stuck in a stale session, choked with dust or reading the game off the wrong drive could easily fall short. Here's how to find out if yours is falling victim to any of these problems.
1. Know what frame rate you should be getting

I've played around 60 hours of GTA 6 in the last week on an original-model PS5 I bought in 2021, and haven't seen too much dipping below 30 fps outside of full-on rampages. There are some drops, though, which aligns with others' findings that it regularly falls slightly under 30 fps during ordinary city drives, and dropped to 23 fps during a grenade launcher test with multiple explosions. The PS5 Pro fares much better, with stress tests finding that it maintains 30 fps for the most part, only dropping to around 24 fps when the player wrecks as many cars as possible all at once.

The Series X, meanwhile, generally holds its 30 fps target but can slip during busy scenes and explosions. The Series S, which renders at 720p internally, struggles quite a bit. It hovers between 25 and 30 fps for most of the game and drops to as low as 20 in busy areas and when vehicles start blowing up, with one explosive scene briefly tanking it to 18 or 19 fps during Kotaku's testing.

Since consoles don't have built-in frame rate counters, the simplest way to monitor fps is to watch for stuttering. If the action gets choppy during firefights, police chases, explosions and pile-ups, your frame rate is dropping, which is somewhat normal for current-gen console hardware. You shouldn't be losing frames during cutscenes or when walking or driving around normally, even on a Series S.

If you are, that's a sign something else is amiss with your console. As for native 40 or 60 fps modes, Rockstar's technology production director Marc Chambers has said that even the PS5 Pro's processor isn't powerful enough, settling a major question about GTA 6's controversial FPS decision.
2. Make sure your game is up to date

Rockstar released GTA 6's first post-launch update on November 23. The patch notes describe fixes for several issues that caused the game to crash, along with bugs that could stall playthroughs, from broken autosaves to story phone calls that wouldn't come through. Nowhere in the patch notes is frame rate or performance mentioned, though. The rumor mill started spinning up shortly after, claiming that Rockstar would push a stuttering fix on November 25, but nothing came of it.

To check whether your game is up to date on PS5, highlight GTA 6 on the main menu, press the Options button on your controller and select Check for Update. Xbox players should go to My games & apps, choose Manage and then check under Updates to see titles that have newer versions available. Storage might be an issue, given the base game's absolutely massive 212GB size. Sony has warned that installing data can require roughly twice as much free space as the install size, so a console that's filled to the brim might refuse to install the patch.

Players were still posting about error CE-108255-1 and others as recently as November 25. Sony describes it, rather vaguely, as an error with a game or application. If it keeps happening after updating, Sony's crash troubleshooting runs through installing the latest system software, starting a new save and, as a last resort, deleting and reinstalling the game.
3. Quit the game instead of resuming it

Quick Resume on the Xbox Series X and S saves the state of a game when you switch to another one, then reloads that state when you come back. It's the feature that enables the frame rate glitch mentioned earlier. It works by setting the console to 60Hz, starting GTA 6, switching to 120Hz on the loading screen, launching a different game and then jumping back in through Quick Resume. This relaunches the game with its cap removed, allowing it to run faster than it's meant to — though it can lead to crashes and bugs.

In testing by Digital Foundry, the uncapped Series X only reached 60 fps when flying a plane with nothing but sky in view. It managed around 40 fps on highways with light traffic, but barely beat 30 in heavier scenes, such as busy streets. It concluded that 60 fps is simply out of reach on current hardware and that although a 40 fps mode with VRR could make sense on Series X, it wouldn't be a clear improvement over the current 30 fps cap.

To get a clean start on Xbox, press the Xbox button, highlight GTA 6, press the Menu button and then select Quit. You can also manually choose which games use Quick Resume through Manage game and add-ons > Quick Resume settings on a game's tile. Microsoft added that feature back in April because Quick Resume doesn't always behave as intended in certain titles (particularly after a game has been inactive for a while).

The PS5, meanwhile, keeps games suspended in rest mode. Thus, closing GTA 6 by highlighting its icon on the main menu, pressing Options and choosing Close Game, or turning the console off completely, achieves the same result. Be sure to save your game regularly since you won't have sleep mode as a fallback.
4. Clean out the dust and give it breathing room

Sony's PS5 safety guide recommends keeping your console roughly 4 inches away from walls, out of closed cabinets or other cramped spaces, and off long-pile carpets. It should also be free of dust on its vents. Microsoft recommends similar for the Xbox: a well-ventilated, relatively cool spot away from heat sources, with nothing sitting on, under or right next to the console. Since both went on sale in late 2020, plenty of consoles have had six years to suck up dust.

While neither Sony nor Microsoft says that a hot console will lead to slower gameplay, heat stress wears components down more quickly. Also, if your PS5 gets too hot, you'll be met with an on-screen warning, at which point Sony recommends switching it off and letting it cool down to prevent damage. On Xbox, meanwhile, poor ventilation and/or overheating is one of two causes Microsoft gives for the console switching itself off without warning. So while a hot console won't necessarily cut the frame rate, it could crash your game or force your console to shut down.

There's also been speculation that overheating could be behind some of the PS5 crashes we've seen since GTA 6's launch. That's possibly because of degradation of the liquid metal that sits between the processor and its cooler. A clean console isn't a workaround for hardware limitations and faults, but it does remove heat as a potential suspect.
Sony says that before cleaning your PS5, you should unplug it and wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth. Its side covers come off, allowing you to clean the dust catchers more easily.
5. Play from the console's internal SSD

GTA 6 needs up to 212GB of free space on both consoles, which is close to a third of the roughly 667GB that's usable on an 825GB PS5. That might push you toward installing the game on a secondary M.2 SSD added to the console's expansion slot. While the PS5 is compatible with a wide range of PCIe Gen4 drives, Sony recommends a sequential read speed of 5,500 MB/s or faster and requires a heatsink or similar cooling. But even with a compatible drive faster than that, games won't necessarily perform the same as they would on the internal SSD.

As you'd expect from such a dense title, the game is constantly pulling in data as you move around Leonida. Digital Foundry's Series S testing found frame rate drops in situations that put a heavy load on the console's AI or streaming, so the game leans on its storage more than others do.

While we haven't seen any examples of GTA 6 behaving problematically when installed on an M.2 drive, if you're doing so and experience stutter when you shouldn't, moving the game back to internal storage is worth a try. On your PS5, go to Settings > Storage > M.2 SSD Storage > Move Games and Apps to move as needed. On an Xbox, Series X and S games can only run from the internal SSD or Microsoft's Storage Expansion Card, which Microsoft says performs identically to the internal drive.

articles.headline: Princess Kate wants people to learn from her cancer journey in vulnerable new documentary
keyFacts: Princess Kate reflects on her cancer journey in a 30-minute documentary titled 'Heal' to raise money for a London hospital.
Kate said her cancer experience profoundly affected every aspect of her life, changing both her physical and emotional well-being.
The documentary will air on NBC on November 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from December 1.
body: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, reveals how cancer treatment terrified and changed her in a very personal documentary she said she hopes will help others reckon with the disease.

In “Heal,” the royal reflects on mortality with an openness and vulnerability that breaks with the royals’ trademark stoicism and reserve, describing the human challenges she faces after her treatment. The normally private princess gives viewers a glimpse — albeit a highly controlled one — of her cancer journey in the 30-minute film, which was produced to raise money for the Royal Marsden Hospital in London, where she received chemotherapy. The film marks a change in the way royals have spoken about their personal lives.

“William and Kate are communicating more directly with the public than ever before and being more open emotionally than we’ve ever seen,” said Emily Nash, NBC News’ royal contributor. “That really, I think, is as a result of her cancer diagnosis. It’s really changed their lives and they want to share what they’ve learned with the world.”

Speaking in London at a special screening of the documentary that will air on NBC on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT before streaming on Peacock from Dec. 1, Kate told reporters that cancer “doesn’t just affect the body. It changes how you think and feel and profoundly affects every aspect of life.”
“I know this personally, and that the journey through and beyond treatment requires more than medicine alone,” she said.
In the film, Kate explains how cancer changed her.
“Once you experience something like that, it’s very hard to go back to the person you were before,” she says.

“Something like cancer strips everything away,” added Kate, who has made cancer support a central part of her work since her illness. “Yes, it’s physical, but it’s emotional too. The things you thought you knew are no longer there. And you do, in a way, lose yourself.”
Rugged British landscapes play a central role in the film. It was simply shot and accompanied by a score by Scottish composer Erland Cooper, who drew inspiration from birdsong and the natural world.

The documentary “also carries with it a deeper message,” she added. “Healing, whether personal or collective, is not just about fixing what is wrong. It is about finding balance in how we live. Between effort and acceptance, between control and trust, between thinking and simply being.”

Kate had already broken with royal tradition when revealing her diagnosis and subsequent remission. Rather than issuing a traditional text statement, she announced she was receiving treatment for the disease in a three-minute video.
Alongside her family, in a sepia-toned follow-up video featuring mellow music, cinematic angles and slow-motion effects, Kate later announced her return to royal duties.

The royals have invited cameras into their lives before, notably in 1969’s “Royal Family” documentary, which showed Queen Elizabeth II behind the scenes, but kept their distance through formality. Kate’s brother- and sister-in-law produced the six-part Netflix documentary series “Harry & Meghan” after they stepped down as working royals.

Both then and now in her latest documentary, Kate has not revealed what type of cancer she was diagnosed with in March 2024 after major abdominal surgery, but in “Heal” she says that the disease changed her.

Talking about her time in the hospital, she says in the film that it was “a really scary, disorientating experience.” On one occasion, she says, the simple act of someone holding her hand made all the difference.

“I think I was sort of in and out of consciousness. It was a really dark time. But also then, somewhere through that too, I became aware of someone holding my hand. They weren’t talking to me. They weren’t trying to fix anything. They were just there. And the presence of someone that stood by me in that time, I’ll forever be grateful for,” she says.
Although she is seen crying at one point when she hears messages of support from her three children, George, Charlotte and Louis, there are also lighter moments.

Part of the film shows Kate completing what is known as the National Three Peaks Challenge, in which she scaled Scafell Pike, Ben Nevis and Snowdon, the highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales, in just 24 hours.

At one point, she plays a game of “Would you rather” with her brother James as they walk, challenging him to pick between two funny and difficult options. She told him she played the game with her children.
Along their journey, she also met up with some hikers and spoke to other people about the challenges they faced fighting cancer.

“You don’t get any help with that from doctors or the language that they use,” one told her. “There are no tools in the clinical settings to kind of help with that. Finding language or finding other people, that community or art or something, these are the only tools we have, I think, to explain and to exercise your uncertainty and become OK with it.”
The film makes no mention of King Charles III, who revealed his own cancer diagnosis in February 2024, a month before Kate.
But the princess said ahead of the film’s release that she hoped it would “encourage compassion, showing the real value in standing alongside one another in the hardest of times.”
“Above all, I hope it helps support the life-changing work of the Royal Marsden and all those navigating life with cancer to ensure no one faces this disease feeling unseen, unsupported or alone.”
